title: Bessent ‘Economic D-Day’ Seen as Warning Shot
summary:
The US “economic D-Day” against Iran turned out to be less Normandy and more Grenada, with Scott Bessent providing few details on how the administration’s new initiative would achieve any of Donald Trump’s desired results, namely the full opening of the Strait of Hormuz.
Dan Tannebaum, Global Anti-Financial Crime Practice Leader at Oliver Wyman, discusses the move from Bessent and how previous threats from the Trump Administration, particularly in the tariff space, compare. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: USD rises after PCE data, recoups half of buyback losses
summary: The dollar rose by the most in nearly four weeks, recovering about half of the losses triggered by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s surprise move last week to prop up the bond market, as inflation data bolstered bets that the Federal Reserve will start raising interest rates by year end.

title: Options Turnover Sinks at India’s Biggest Exchange
summary: Options turnover on India’s biggest stock exchange fell to the lowest this year on monthly expiry day, reflecting the impact of the stricter trading rules and the introduction of the closing-auction system in the world’s largest equity derivatives market.

Wall Street traders sent bonds lower and stocks wavered, with the latest economic reports doing little to alter bets the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates this year.

title: Modest Inflation, Soft Spending Support Fed Hold
summary:
July’s personal income and outlays report indicates the underlying pace of inflation increased relatively modestly. 
Real spending also came in soft. The weakness was exaggerated by temporary factors such as the earlier-than-usual Amazon Prime Day, but the concentration of spending in essentials suggests the underlying pace of spending has decelerated.
Michael Ball, Macro Strategist with Bloomberg News, reacts to the PCE data. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: JM Smucker Rises on Outlook; Intuit Down on Full-Year Forecast | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Intuit (INTU) shares are down after the tax-preparation software company gave a full-year forecast for both adjusted earnings and revenue that was weaker than expected.
- Abercrombie & Fitch (ANF) is climbing as it raised its outlook for the year after logging higher second-quarter profit and sales, driven by improving demand across multiple geographies.
- JM Smucker (SJM) shares are rising as it raised its full-year outlook for sales and profit, buoyed by growth in its Uncrustables sandwiches and coffee. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Hundreds Missing After Deadly Nepal-China Flood
summary: A violent flash flood at the border between Nepal and China has left hundreds missing, including tourists from India, the US, UK and elsewhere. (Source: Bloomberg)
